question.problem: The lifetime of a certain type of electrical switch varies continuously. Lifetime of different switches of this type are independent, and switches replacements have a constant average rate of one every $2$ years. Determine the probability that a switch fails between the first and the second year. Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.

current_example.problem: At an electronics store, smartphone purchases occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate of one sale every $20$ minutes. Rounded to four decimal places, what is the probability that the next smartphone is sold within the next $5$ minutes?
current_example.worked_solution:
Since the purchases occur continuously in time, independently, and at a constant average rate, we can model the time until the next purchase as an exponential distribution.

An exponential random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134435/assets/5816d7625f5ed354da1e0b35aa7d66226b4197c3376bff2d73ea964074f4e47c.svg)

Let $X$ be the amount of time until the next smartphone is purchased. Since there is a purchase every $20$ minutes on average, the rate is $\lambda = 1/20$ purchases per minute.

The time intervals between successive purchases can be modeled as an exponential random variable with rate $\lambda = 1/20,$ and we can write 

$$
X\sim \textrm{Exp} \left( \dfrac{1}{20} \right).
$$

So, $X$ has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14134435/assets/fff5956e4c99d8e8612b552e341c6f17a23d3ba870ca82cd20e3ae99560f824f.svg)

Therefore, the probability that a customer will purchase a smartphone within the next $5$ minutes is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<5) & ={\int }_{0}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{5}\frac{1}{20}{e}^{-x/20}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-{e}^{-x/20}|}_{0}^{5} \\  & =-{e}^{-1/4}+{e}^{0} \\  & =1-{e}^{-1/4} \\  & ≈0.2212\,.\end{aligned}
$$
